hackernews.author: westurner
hackernews.body:
Attention Is Not What You Need (2025)
The author describes the model's pairing operation as:
(zt,zt+Delta) where Delta is a positive offset.
This means the model is using the next token to predict the next token. It should have been (zt,zt-Delta), or it's cheating.
I don't know if that's just the paper, or if the code was also b0rk3d. I agree with the framing but the claim is too strong.
I don't think Grassmannian manifolds are necessarily a better representation than simple query/key inner products. It's a valid solution, and it does have advantages in some cases.
The Grassmannian is only preserving the subspace orientation, so ... Scale is all you need.
That's why you see other attention free large language models work. But in a world with constraints on time and compute the architecture does matter because scaling does have a cost (which is dropping)

comment_insights: The author describes the model's pairing operation as:
I agree with the framing but the claim is too strong.

My gut (informed by 30ish years of professional hardware and software engineering) says implemented at scale, on a real machine, we start seeing the same performance issues functional languages have w
There are many alternatives to attention which work well for small sequence sizes.
